en: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
[I praise] Him whose qualities are extolled by the lords of heaven and earth,
who is unborn by nature, yet born as the supreme sun within the solar dynasty.
He saw the Lord of the Raghus, praised by the gods, who was increasing the prosperity of his own home like the lord of the stars (the moon), and who, accompanied by Sītā, was bowing with joy. || 1 ||
Like a Śaiva bow that destroys the sugarcane, he was the subduer of the host of kings on the path by means of the drawn string of the preeminent Bhṛgu;
thereafter, he enjoyed the pure domestic life of a householder.
[He saw] Raghunātha, who is accompanied by Sītā, who is full of bliss, who is bowed to, and who is praised by the gods. || 2 ||
Having received the command of his guru, he followed him into the forest together with his wife and Lakṣmaṇa, renouncing even the desired royal happiness of the gods;
[he protected] her whose mind was consumed by the agony of separation from her beloved due to the hideous Rākṣasī.
Together with Sītā, full of joy, he bowed before the Lord of the Raghus, who is praised by the gods. || 3 ||
Having brought Virādha to heaven and thereafter Kabandha— the enemy of the gods—
to the shore of Pampā, he experienced the joy of meeting the son of the Wind;
then, having gone to Kiṣkindhā, he recognized Sugrīva and his ministers as being endowed with noble qualities.
Together with Sītā and filled with joy, he bowed down before the Lord of the Raghus, who is praised by the gods. || 4 ||
Longing for his beloved, having reached the ocean with his monkey hosts,

he who built a bridge over the waters and was the slayer of the race of asuras— the sinless one who gazed upon the pure Sītā, half of whose body was offered into the fire, and who remained as immovable as a mountain.
Together with Sītā, full of joy, he bowed before the Lord of the Raghus, who is praised by the gods. || 5 ||
Having ascended the celestial chariot, he went to Ayodhyā— where his feet are served by his younger brothers and Sītā— and attained the eternal station of kingship,
satisfying the gods with his own mouth through excellent sacrifices, his mind being perfectly tranquil.
[He saw] Raghunātha, who was with Sītā and filled with joy, who had bowed down, and who was praised by the gods. || 6 ||

He who ordains progeny, the sustainer of all, who establishes beings in their respective duties, who is the path of the Vedas and the embodiment of right conduct, who performs everything ordained by the Vedas,
and who bestows an abundance of love upon men while acting for the welfare of all humanity.
Accompanied by Satī and Ānanda, he bowed down before Raghunātha, who is praised by the gods.
Having learned that he will indeed depart from this world without returning, the foremost of the twice-born shall cross over the entire darkness by means of hearing and reciting his fame.

Therefore, having established him there, he joyfully led back to his own city the entire host of supplicants, along with Sītā, as they bowed before the Lord of the Raghus, who is praised by the gods. || 8 ||
This heart-pleasing Raghunāthāṣṭaka was composed by Raghunātha; it destroys the heap of sins for those who recite it and bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Thus ends the *Śrīraghunāthāṣṭaka*, composed by the scholar Śrī Śivadatta Miśra Śāstrī.
